description:
FOUND s454ae by probe while fixing the census try-family (Test2::Util try returns ($ok, $err); the shifted list swapped the two).  MINIMIZED (scratch p8.pl): sub t4 { my $ok = eval { die "z\n" }; return ($ok, "w") } my ($m, $n) = t4();  perl: m=undef n=w.  PCL: m=w n=undef.  DISCRIMINATORS ALREADY MEASURED: return (undef, "x") is CORRECT; my $u; return ($u, "y") is CORRECT; only the eval-died-result scalar drops out -- so the bug is the REPRESENTATION eval leaves in the scalar (likely an empty-list/(values) marker that p-flatten-args elides when the sub result flattens), not undef handling in general.  Runtime family (cl/ or the return lowering); a cl/ change means the full sweep per the WHAT-TO-RUN table.  Fix bar: the three-probe set above vs perl + a Pl/t guard row; check the (&;@)-block-form spelling too (sub t(&;@) probe p7.pl).

DONE s456ag (Opus agent AG, round 13).  ONE LINE, in the right layer: p-return-value's
scalar-box arm (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) now normalises a box whose value is raw nil to
*p-undef*.  The task's diagnosis was exactly right -- raw nil IS the runtime's
"empty list" marker (%p-flatten-list's `((null item) nil)` arm drops it BY DESIGN,
and that arm must stay: array holes and Exporter's hash-export internals ride on it),
and p-return-value unboxed a scalar straight into it.

WHY ONLY `return`: every OTHER list consumer receives the BOX (p-flatten-list snapshots
it), so `my @a = ($ok,"w")`, `push`, `join`, `foo($ok,"w")`, `%h = ($ok,"w")` and the
IMPLICIT return (a sub whose last form is the list) were all already correct -- measured,
10 shapes.  p-return-value is called from p-return and nowhere else, so the blast radius
is exactly the explicit-return path.

THE FAMILY IS BIGGER THAN THE EVAL: any scalar that came to hold raw nil vanished the
same way.  Measured producers: `my $ok = eval { die }` and `sub g { return } my $ok = g()`
(bare return in SCALAR context yields nil).  `my $u;`, `= undef`, `$h{missing}`, `$e[3]`,
`= f()` where f does `return undef` all yield *p-undef* already and were never affected.
Single-element `return ($ok)` was ALSO broken (n=0 where perl says 1) and is fixed by the
same line.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3, all identical after the fix: the task's three-probe set; 9 shapes
of "where did the nil come from"; 10 consumer shapes; 19 shapes the change could BREAK
(empty array in list AND scalar ctx, bare return, `return ()`, `return $undef`, empty
hash, arrayref/scalarref/coderef/blessed returns, undef+array, undef+empty-array,
numeric and string use of a returned undef, a return of a sub call's result); and the
(&;@) block-form spelling the task asked for (`sub tryit (&;@) {...} my ($ok,$err) =
tryit { die "boom\n" }`).

GUARD: Pl/t/list-scalar-context-01.t 27 -> 31 rows.  Three of the four FAIL on the base
tree (inverse-run with the one line reverted); the fourth is the inverse row (empty array
/ bare return / () still contribute 0) and passes on both by design.

TARGETED SWEEP (cl/ change): perl-tests eval.t context.t sub.t wantarray.t args.t
aassign.t -- fail rows byte-identical to baselines/fail-baseline.tsv for all six.
eval.t shows 8 NEW / 4 GONE rows against the blessed baseline, but the SAME 8/4 appear
with the fix REVERTED (run alone, --jobs 1): pre-existing baseline drift in an
INCOMPLETE file, not this change.  A cl/ change owes a FULL sweep -- Fable runs it over
the merged batch.
subject: A scalar holding a died eval\x27s result VANISHES from a returned list: `my $ok = eval { die "z\n" }; return ($ok, "w")` returns ("w") where perl returns (undef, "w") -- list assignment then shifts left, silent wrong
